Releasing RdistNN

Source: RELEASING.md

Supported workflows include CATE, nonparametric regression, supplied-prediction CLATE and ordinary paired-signal ratios, with DNN weights, pointwise jackknife uncertainty, tuning, diagnostics and plots. Ratio confidence-set inversion, PLQR and local IV-GMM remain experimental.

Version 0.1.3 replaces the 0.1.2 identical-covariate rule with target-specific exact represented distance averaging. Earlier saved fits require refitting. Preserve all historical tags, assets and scientific dependency pins when publishing this release.

Version progression

The first development commit after production 0.1.x establishes 0.1.x.9000. Increment its fourth component in each subsequent development commit, even a small documentation or implementation change. Drafting a version in uncommitted changes does not advance this sequence. Read the current version from DESCRIPTION and the current NEWS.md heading; keep them synchronized. For example, development after production 0.1.2 starts at 0.1.2.9000, then 0.1.2.9001.

For each production merge, default to 0.1.(x+1) unless the maintainer explicitly selects another version. Prepare that production version in the reviewed candidate before merging, then start the next development cycle by appending .9000 to the selected production version. Thus the current default cycle leads to production 0.1.3, followed by development 0.1.3.9000. Production merging, tagging and asset publication remain separate authorized steps. Retain full commit and checked-archive identities alongside version numbers.

Production history

Version 0.1.2 entered production master through the reviewed squash merge of PR #20 on 2026-10-22 at c96878562f105a22290edf989631f197d9735e1c. It adds duplicate-covariate block averaging and deletion-aware survivor weights, with a theory warning; see NEWS.md. Production source publication does not itself create a version tag or replace GitHub release assets.

The 0.1.1 baseline combines numerical fixes, canonical covariate tie ordering, shared implementation modules and a current-only interface, aligned with the Stata companion. Earlier development fit schemas and obsolete aliases require refitting with current syntax. The previous version 0.1.0.9004 entered production master through the reviewed squash merge of PR #16 at 3394ae55383ffa4cb6bfad909730378dd8c7d4cb, aligned with the Stata companion. Version 0.1.0.9003 identifies the previous production snapshot. The exact-table recurrence, compensated reductions, numerical origins, shared covariance and fitted whitening policy first shipped in the merged 0.1.0.9003 snapshot, not 0.1.0.9002. See NEWS.md. A verified candidate requires the final-source checks below. Public tags and assets require separate authorization. Keep the selected production version throughout its final verification and merge; ongoing development commits follow the policy above. Matching R/Stata versions do not imply identical feature coverage.

Review the known asymptotic-tail limitation in the numerical reference when assessing a candidate. Engine agreement on fixed tables does not establish correct construction or cross-language support parity at subnormal scales. Check that generated Rplots.pdf files, including nested outputs, remain excluded from the source package.

Candidate identity and scientific reproduction

The current version-pinned R release is v0.1.3. The tag selects the verified production snapshot; its installable source package and checksum file are attached to the release. Install with:

pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN@v0.1.3")

The tag fixes the installation source at the released commit. Keep the ordinary README installation on production master and retain historical tags, assets and paper dependency pins. Record the paired final commits and asset checksums in the release-set manifest below.

Commit candidates locally. Publish review branches/PRs, tags, downloadable assets and websites only when authorized; do not push directly to master. After both package commits are final, bind them in one external release-set manifest under ignored outputs. Include tested trees, artifact filenames, sizes and SHA-256, commands, runtime/compiler information, hosted run IDs/tested SHAs and explicit PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN gates. Do not create circular committed HEAD references or embed an archive’s own hash inside it.

For a historical reference, install the previous immutable 0.1.0.9004 source with:

pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN@3394ae55383ffa4cb6bfad909730378dd8c7d4cb")

The unpinned README command follows production master; @v0.1.0 selects the existing older public tag. The 0.1.0.9004 source update and pkgdown deployment did not create a new tag or replace the v0.1.0 release assets. Historical source snapshots shared development versions; retain their full commit or checked archive identity. Current development commits follow the increment policy above.

For an unpublished future candidate, check out its full recorded commit in a separate local checkout and use pak::local_install("."), or install its checked tarball. Put exact candidate commands in the external handoff once both final identities are known.

The paper-evidence renderer verifies accepted stored bytes and reconstructs 21 tables and six figures. It does not run the candidate estimator. Simulation freezes bind source commit 40060f155cc4d84d59ee5af119f6a2534c569bab, a source override and a native-library hash. SIPP binds installed files and its DLL; its recorded sibling checkout alone does not identify the loaded package. Preserve both historical records. Historical recomputation requires the matching dependency. Fresh launchers use and record actual installed software; outputs require review before promotion. Candidate agreement does not change the historical reproduction reference. See the installed bundle README.

Use Rscript --vanilla tools/replication/compare_paper_dependency.R --help for bounded validation with explicit installations, file-hashed identities and a frozen case manifest declaring quantity-specific budgets. Fresh processes compare fixed-table arithmetic, exact-table construction and geometry separately. Retained SIPP arrays stay private; dependency comparison requires neither forest refitting nor production simulation.

Prepare and verify the final source

Run from the repository root with package dependencies and development tools installed as described in CONTRIBUTING.md.

  1. Confirm that DESCRIPTION and the current NEWS.md entry agree. Check the chosen tag only for a separately authorized public release. Synchronize README and website draft references, while preserving historical release notes. Regenerate help and README from their sources:

    devtools::document()
devtools::build_readme()

  2. Run the alignment checks in CONTRIBUTING.md, then build the installable source package with all vignettes and check that exact archive:

    dir.create("archives", showWarnings = FALSE)
src <- devtools::build(path = "archives", vignettes = TRUE, manual = FALSE)
rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck(
  src, args = "--no-manual", error_on = "warning",
  check_dir = "archives/check"
)

    Investigate all errors and warnings, and review any notes. Inspect the archive’s file list: it should contain package code, generated help, tests, and built vignettes, while excluding private notes, agent settings, CI logs, prior archives, and repository-only publication instructions. archives/ is ignored and excluded from future source builds.

    Run the full source suite with devtools::test() as well (including checkout-only documentation contracts), mirrored-header checks and focused compiled/forced-R numerical/consumer regressions from tests/README.md. Install this exact archive in a fresh library, execute installed examples, and run its paper-replication verify.R and render_evidence.R --output-dir=NEW_DIR. Verify exports, the installed bundle, accepted table reconstruction and unchanged installed files afterward. Record rendering separately from estimator recomputation.

  3. Build the documentation site, including examples and articles:

    pkgdown::build_site()

    Review docs/index.html, docs/articles/getting-started.html, and docs/reference/index.html. Verify that CATE and regression lead the onboarding, supported CLATE is described under its inference conditions, and confidence-set inversion, PLQR and IV-GMM retain experimental labels. The generated docs/ directory is ignored. The canonical site URL is https://JakobJuergens.github.io/RdistNN/.

  4. Review the final diff. Require passing R-CMD-check on Linux, Windows, macOS arm64, and macOS x86-64 for the release commit, plus the alignment checks. CI also covers R release, devel, and oldrel on Linux. Local checks do not substitute for this platform matrix. Reuse successful validation while the source snapshot is unchanged.

Publish on GitHub

Create the chosen v<version> tag and GitHub release from the verified commit. Use the release-scope section of NEWS.md for the introduction, followed by a link to the getting-started guide and the explicit PLQR experimental status.

Attach RdistNN_<version>.tar.gz, built above, as the installable R source asset. GitHub’s automatically generated repository ZIP/tarball and the CI source-snapshot ZIP are repository snapshots; the R source package includes built vignettes and applies .Rbuildignore exclusions. Include a checksum:

cd archives
rdistnn_release_version=$(Rscript -e 'cat(read.dcf("../DESCRIPTION")[1L, "Version"])')
sha256sum "RdistNN_${rdistnn_release_version}.tar.gz" > SHA256SUMS

After publication, download both assets without credentials and run sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS from their download directory. Install the downloaded tarball in a fresh library and execute the getting-started examples. For version-pinned GitHub installation, use pak::pak("JakobJuergens/RdistNN@v<version>"), replacing <version> with the published version; the default branch remains available for development installations.

Users can install a downloaded source asset with the actual version in its filename:

install.packages("Rcpp")  # required dependency, if not already installed
install.packages("RdistNN_<version>.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")

Source installation needs C++17. Optional visualization requires ggplot2 (and patchwork for dashboards); other suggested dependencies support development, replication, or experimental workflows.

Publishing a GitHub release triggers .github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml, which builds the site and deploys it to gh-pages. Confirm that this workflow succeeds and GitHub Pages serves that branch before announcing the public documentation links. A manual run of the same workflow can refresh the site without a release. Neither local site building nor pushing package sources alone deploys the site.

Introduce the package on jakobjuergens.com

WEBSITE.md contains a short software entry and release announcement ready to copy into the website’s existing format. Link to the GitHub release and canonical documentation site after both are live. Keep the package documentation on its canonical URL rather than duplicating its reference pages on the personal site. Review both links after publication.

This file records publication steps; preparing files or building the local site does not itself tag, publish, or deploy a release.
